facts.text: Mazie was established in a region originally within the Cherokee Nation's Saline District before European-American settlement intensified.
The area around Mazie retains historical Amish and Mennonite influences, contributing to a community emphasis on traditional values and self-sufficiency.
Mazie emerged as an unincorporated community during the late territorial period, influenced by the Dawes Act of 1887.
A local post office opened on July 11, 1905, serving as a key hub for correspondence and supplies in Mazie.
Early settlement patterns in Mazie emphasized farming, with Cherokee families cultivating crops like corn and beans.
The land encompassing present-day Mazie was originally part of the traditional territory of the Osage Nation in the early 19th century.
